description: Task 024 — Renovate activation. Runner is the Mend hosted GitHub App.
Tier 1 = PRs open freely (leaf application images).
Tier 2 = dependencyDashboardApproval (control plane, CNI, databases, the
GitOps engine, platform Helm charts) — drift is reported, a human ticks a
box to get a PR at all.
Tier 3 = dashboard approval AND a CI guard: sops/uv carry a sibling
_sha256 that a version-only bump leaves stale, so scripts/pin-guard.sh
fails such a PR closed. terraform has no checksum coupling — its
constraint is live-state parity and is not CI-enforceable.
schedule limits when PRs may be raised, not when drift is discovered.
automerge is deliberately set nowhere: every bump is a human merge.

customManagers.description: npm CLI + orchestrator toolchain pins in the dev workstation ansible role
cluster component pins in the k3s/rke2 ansible roles

pinned tool + chart-value versions (CI workflows, ArgoCD values). Two matchStrings: a bare version value, and an image reference whose tag is the version. They are mutually exclusive — a bare version may not contain ':' or '/', an image reference must contain ':'.

packageRules.description: Never touch self-referencing GitOps branch refs — targetRevision: main on Applications pointing at this same repo is not an upstream version
MinIO date-stamped tags need custom versioning
Tier 3 — checksum-coupled: each *_version has a sibling *_sha256. A version-only PR fails scripts/pin-guard.sh by design
Tier 3 — terraform: live-state parity. Never bump past the version that wrote the live state without a verified zero-diff plan. Not CI-enforceable

Tier 2 — databases: a bump is a restart. matchPackageNames is an exact match, so every spelling a manifest may use is listed — the dry run caught cloudflared escaping this gate because that manifest writes the registry prefix and the rule did not
Tier 2 — GitOps engine and edge: ksops decrypts everything, cloudflared is the only ingress
Group CI action patches — cannot reach the cluster
